findings.title: The documented string-literal residual recreates the element-replacement false green
findings.body: Quoted contents are still interpreted as structure. With `<input placeholder="}" autoFocus={true}/>` the quoted `}` leaves `depth` positive, so `openTagAt` misses `<input>` and emits the unqualified `autoFocus` key. Replacing `input` with `textarea` produces the same fingerprint and count, and the gate exits successfully. A quoted `>` similarly returns `null`. The claimed “stable” result is therefore a stable collision, not a harmless one-time baseline change; it directly violates the accepted owning-element discriminator contract. The `}` case is also introduced by 0990d67: the preceding raw scan would still identify `input`.
findings.recommendation: Use a JSX parser/tokenizer or a quote-aware scan that handles quoted attribute values and escapes. Add an `input`→`textarea` fixture with `placeholder="}"` that must fail, plus literal-only edits that must pass.

findings.title: The comparison regression test cannot fail on the pre-fix bug
findings.body: `openTagAt` scans only source preceding the diagnosed `autoFocus` span, but this fixture places `disabled={count < name}` after `autoFocus`. The comparison is therefore never inspected; the pre-0990d67 implementation also identifies `Input` and passes this test. Although the current code resolves the correctly ordered reproduction, the committed test does not protect the second accepted R3-F1 case in this repeatedly defective function.
findings.recommendation: Place `disabled={count < name}` before `autoFocus`, retain the variable-rename PASS assertion, and verify that reverting to the pre-fix scanner makes this test fail.
